# V11 — Apparent multiyear reproductive memory can be generated by fixed individual quality

**2026-10-10 / mina PR193 / method and source-eligibility investigation only.** This is NOT a new empirical discovery about penguin behavior; no penguin-level outcomes were read. Frozen Ecology manuscript PR189 and USAP official-mark–resight PR142 untouched.

## Why the previously proposed colony recovery mechanism still lacks an identified cause

Ainley et al. (2024; doi:10.1017/S0954102024000051) have already assessed Cape Royds' long-term lack of recovery after the iceberg era, implicating Ross Gyre changes, open-water access, skua predation and more. Lescroël et al. (2009; doi:10.1111/j.1365-2656.2009.01542.x) already quantified the transition from successful / unsuccessful / nonbreeding reproductive states at Cape Crozier and found that successful breeders were more likely to succeed again and survive (estimated survival 0.76 vs 0.67 for their compared states). Their multistate GOF **Where Before, Where After** component was non-ideal (**χ²=24.22, df=12, p=0.02**), leading to overdispersion correction. This is a possible model-misspecification/history warning, **not proof of genuinely higher-order individual memory or a new cause**. Dugger et al. (2010; doi:10.1073/pnas.1000623107) already showed breeder movements under iceberg stress increasing from generally under 1% to ~3.5% at Royds; Dugger et al. (2026; doi:10.3389/fevo.2026.1868960) already modeled 25 years of colony- and age-dependent pre-breeder and breeder movement, sabbatical participation and reproductive recruitment. Both movement and breeder participation are therefore studied, not new effects.

## Mathematical negative control with NO actual penguin data

A latent quality mixture can induce a large apparent second-order effect even if **each animal has zero state dependence**:

- Half of birds are permanently 'higher quality' and have independent per-year breeding success probability **0.8**; half are permanently 'lower quality' and have probability **0.2**.
- A bird that succeeded **two times in a row** has a posterior 16/17 probability of high quality, and its next success probability is **13/17 ≈ 0.7647**.
- A bird that **failed then succeeded** has a posterior 1/2 probability of high quality, and its next success probability is **0.5**.
- Both birds have exactly the SAME **current success** state; the older state appears to predict a difference **9/34 ≈ 0.2647**, although the model has **NO biological memory, recovery debt, or carry-over**.
- Symmetrically, within currently failed birds, earlier success seems predictive by the same magnitude. Conditioning on past observations simply updates knowledge of persistent individual type.

The exact fraction is reproduced by source-free [GitHub Actions #38012309821](https://github.com/zuizui0223/mina/actions/runs/38012309821), using `scripts/prove_reproductive_frailty_second_order_aliasing_v11.py` and tests. This is **a known mixture-model/latent-frailty phenomenon**, not a new theorem or an observed Antarctic result. A significant longer-history regression cannot alone distinguish true learned/social/physiological memory from selection on stable unmeasured individual quality.

## A prospective and realistically testable distinction — but original data blocked

The public [Kappes et al. 2020 Dryad data](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.s7h44j15w) were used for the 2021 age-related performance paper (doi:10.1111/1365-2656.13422). Dryad advertises `BreedingSuccess.csv` (~328 kB) with recoded `ID, colony, season, success, breeder, age, afr, afrc, expt, expl, alr` across 1997–2013 at **Bird, Crozier and Royds, all three on Ross Island**. Success explicitly records **fledged chick** vs failed nest for breeding birds, and nonbreeding means no breeding behavior observed, **not independently verified absence/alive**. The dataset's author notes explicitly ask to contact Point Blue/Grant Ballard before detailed novel reanalyses, and warn that recoded IDs **must not be joined to IDs released for other papers**, including the official 2026 Ross study.

We froze source-schema eligibility *before* opening any new individual data: `contracts/ADELIE_MULTIGENERATION_REPRODUCTIVE_STATE_MEMORY_SOURCE_GATE_V11.json`. The public file's exact official downloadable hyperlink was `https://datadryad.org/downloads/file_stream/532106`. A bounded **first-header-only** [GitHub Action #38012233947](https://github.com/zuizui0223/mina/actions/runs/38012233947) completed success as a source audit but got **HTTP 403 Forbidden**. **Zero actual penguin IDs or outcomes were read; no model fit.** No unofficial URL, invented schema or mirror was substituted.

If authorized original source becomes available and authors can advise on quality/detection, the right comparison would be:
1. Fit age, colony×year, current breeder state, true observed alive/at-risk, within-bird latent frailty and detection/absence structure with **first-order** last breeding history.
2. Only then test whether second/third prior outcomes offer **held-out-year** predictive value beyond that model, with temporal ordering fixed *before* outcomes, not after.
3. Attempt independently replicated histories from **separate geographic islands**. Three named 'colonies' all located on Ross Island are not three independent islands; even a robust within-Ross result does not independently test an island-boundary colonization mechanism.
4. A predictive improvement would still not establish *causal* memory unless stable individual quality and time-varying individual condition are disentangled using additional information or an independent natural perturbation; otherwise label as conditional predictive history.

## Scientific gate / recommendation

**CURRENT: HOLD_OFFICIAL_DRYAD_403_AND_NO_INDEPENDENT_CAUSAL_HETEROGENEITY_IDENTIFICATION.** There is a real, relatively self-contained published longitudinal author dataset with an explicit original long-history warning; but no accessible original data file in the current workflow and no justified new causal claim. The frailty counterexample also demonstrates why fitting a positive lagged slope to the known 36 Crozier nests or historical Ross age-status records and calling it ecological memory would be misleading. Use the available source only after following original author usage advice, under a genuinely new agreed scientific question.

A new island-biogeography mechanism remains unconfirmed. The strongest *necessary data improvement* is independent individual identities and dated nest success across separate islands, with true survey nonobservations separated from alive nonbreeding birds, and a source-timed perturbation of disperser arrival/access or cue availability. No fabricated p-values, fecundity or source-colony moves.
